Having sprinkled the fuel for the fire three times, he pours out the remainder, places that vessel to the south, and puts the two strainers into the full vessel. Taking the full vessel and reciting as before, he carries it level with his breath and sets it down on *darbha* grass to the north of the fire; having covered it with *darbha* grass, [he prepares] for the sake of the *brahmā*.
Having seated the Brahman priest to the south of the fire on the Darbha grass, or in the absence of that [grass], in the place of the Brahman.

In this fire-sacrifice (*homakarman*), having given the seat of the Brahman priest with the formula, "O Brahman, become the Brahman; O Brahman, you are the Brahman," and having placed the two strainers (*pavitra*) into the vessel of clarified butter (*ājyapātra*), having melted the clarified butter, having poured the clarified butter onto the strainers placed to the west of the fire, having drawn out embers toward the north, having placed [the vessel] upon them, having purified the clarified butter by waving a burning blade of grass over it, having cut off two blades of *darbha* grass, having washed them, having thrown them back [into the fire], and having touched water, he should carry fire around the *caru* three times.

Having cast out the embers toward the north and swept them back, he heats the clarified butter (*ājya*) three times with the two strainers (*pavitra*) whose tips point north; having loosened the knot of the strainers, washed them, and placed them in the fire with their tips pointing east, he throws them into the fire along with the *darbha* grass. Then, taking the *sruva* ladle with his right hand and the *juhū* spoon with his left, he heats them simultaneously. Holding the *juhū* at the junction of the left little finger and ring finger, he places the *sruva* over it so that its opening faces inward, its hollow facing all directions, and its handle aligned with the base of the *darbha* roots.

Having held the *vyutkramaṇa* [grass-blade], he cleanses the *juhū* with the tips [of the blades] facing inward, the middle parts facing east, and the bases facing west—thus cleansing the *dara* [ladle] in sequence with the *darbha* grasses from the *sruva*. He touches each blade as it is being cleansed, one after another. Then, taking the fuel (*idhma*), he lays the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) around: the thickest is the middle one; the southern one is thinner and longer; the northern one is the thinnest and shortest. The middle one has its tip pointing north, while the other two have their tips pointing east. The middle one...

Having touched the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), he places two *āghāra* fuel-sticks upright in the east; he sprinkles water around the fire with the formula, "O Aditi, be well-disposed" in the south, facing east; "Do thou likewise be well-disposed" in the west, facing north; "O Sarasvatī, do thou likewise be well-disposed" in the north, facing east; and "O God Savitṛ, impel [the sacrifice]" all around. Having adorned the fuel-wood (*idhma*), having adorned himself, and having adorned the Brahman priest, and having twice poured clarified butter over the fuel-wood, placing it between the middle of the root and the middle [of the trunk], in this sacrificial rite...

"O Brahman, I shall lay the fuel; do you authorize me. Being thus authorized, he sits down and silently lays this fuel with both hands, saying, "To Prajāpati, this! He throws the fuel and remains silent for a moment so that it may become well-kindled. He causes it to flame up as at the New and Full Moon sacrifices, silently. Taking the other *darvī* (ladle), he places it within the junction of the northern enclosing stick.

Meditating upon Prajāpati with his mind, he pours a continuous, straight stream from the south toward the east, from the Vāyavya corner to the Āgneya corner, saying: "To Prajāpati, this! Taking the primary ladle, he brings the second [ladle]—dedicated to Indra—down along the junction of the other enclosing-stick, and as before, he pours it out toward the northeast, from the Nairṛti corner to the Īśāna corner, saying: "To Indra, this! Then he offers two portions of clarified butter from the two ladles: to the north, saying "To Agni, svāhā! and to the east, saying "To Agni, this! To Soma, svāhā!"

For the sake of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) and for the sake of the eastern portion, he offers this equally with the preceding [portion] into the central fire, according to the instruction, after having offered the principal oblations (*pradhānāhutīḥ*).
Of the Sun—with the black dust of the sun-grasping demon... beholding, svāhā! This is for the sun-grasping demon.
Agni, the messenger... svāhā! This is for Agni.
To the heart of Rudra, the terrible one... svāhā! This is for Rudra.
For the eclipse of the Moon:
*Oṃ āpyāyasva...* [and so forth] ... *gandhe svāhā*. This is for the eclipse of the Moon.
Oṃ apsume asrākṣi... ṣajī svāhā; this is for the waters.
Oṃ, [I offer] this Gaurī... svāhā; this is for Gaurī.
For Aṅgāraka: "O Kuja, the sage of the planet, Agni is your head... [he] quickens, svāhā! To the planet Aṅgāraka, who is this..."
O pleasant Earth, spread yourself wide... Svāhā! This is for the Earth.
Svāhā to the sight of the field; this is for Kṣetrapālaka.
For Budha: O planet Budha, having awakened... [fill in] ...svāhā. This is for the planet Budha.
Idam vi...sure svāhā; this is for Viṣṇu.
Sahasraśīrṣāya gulam svāhā; this is for Nārāyaṇa.
To Bṛhaspati—the preceptor planet, the sage Bṛhaspati...
[O] Citra, Svāhā! To this planet Bṛhaspati, this [offering].
Brahmajijñā...vivaḥ svāhā; this is for Brahman.
Indra vo ... valiṃ svāhā; this is for Indra.
For Śukra:
"O planet Śukra, may this oblation be for you; Svāhā! This is for the planet Śukra."
O Indrāṇī, [you are] the wife of Indra; svāhā! This is for Indrāṇī.
The sacrifices [are offered] to Indra accompanied by the Maruts; Svāhā! This [is for] Indra accompanied by the Maruts.
For Śanaiścara: "O planet Śani, O sage, O pacifier of fire... [śrīdhraḥ] svāhā! This is for the planet Śanaiścara."
To Yama ... [this] has been offered, svāhā! To Yama, this!
To Prajāpati, [the lord] of ... [the creatures], Svāhā! This is for Prajāpati.
To Rāhu, the planet, [this oblation] is offered...
Svāhā! To this planet Rāhu, this [is given].
The cow that brings prosperity... [grant] strength; Svāhā! This is for the cow.
May there be peace for [the name]... obeisance, svāhā! This is for the serpent.
Of Ketu—having made Ketu the planet and the banner... svāhā! This is for the host of Ketus.
Sacitra ... vasya svāhā; this is for Citragupta.
To the Brahmadevas... svāhā; this is for Brahmā.
*durgāya jātavedase* ... *ity agnaye svāhā*; this [is] for Durgā.
To Gaṇapati, the leader of the hosts... [the most excellent one], svāhā! This is for Gaṇapati.
To Kṣetrapālaka Lakunaku, for the sight of the field... svāhā! This is for Kṣetrapālaka.
O maker of fearlessness, O giver of well-being...
[who makes] happiness, svāhā! This is for the Maker of Fearlessness.
Indrasya indraṃ vo ... valaḥ svāhā; to Indra, the world-protector, this [offering].
Agniṃ agniṃ dūt... taṅ svāhā; [this is] for Agni, the world-protector, this [offering].
May the Nirṛtis,
the stealers and the destroyers, together with the disease-protectors who are here, [be appeased] with Svāhā!
To Varuṇa, indeed, this [cake] of mine... svāhā! This is for Varuṇa, the guardian of the world.
To Vāyu, the wind-god, [and] to Mahā-vāyu, svāhā! This [is for] Vāyu, the world-protector.
To Kubera, the son of Soma... to him, Svāhā! To this Kubera, the guardian of the world (lokapālaka), [this offering].
To that Īśāna, the sovereign lord... svāhā! This [is for] Īśāna, the guardian of the world.
Upwards, upwards... mah svāhā; this is for the Upward-Person (Ūrdhvapuruṣa).
The earth is pleasant... [to us]... to the earth, svāhā; this is for the earth.
To the Vāstupuruṣa, O Lord of the Dwelling... svāhā! This is for the Vāstupuruṣa.
To Brahmā, the god of the Brahmins... svāhā; this is for Brahmā.
To Sarasvatī, for the impelling of the goddess... let her protect; svāhā! This is for Sarasvatī.
Viṣṇu: "idaṃ viṣṇur... ... svāhā; this [is for] Śrī Mahāviṣṇu.
As one winnows chaff from grain, [so may Lakṣmī be removed]... Svāhā! This is for Śrī Mahālakṣmī.
To Rudra for the heart that is difficult to appease, svāhā! This is for Rudra.
Gaurī, Gaurī amā... [mantra] svāhā; this is for Gaurī.
To the Aśvins, the deities, who have performed this for the infant... O Aśvins, [this is] the great *svāhā*! To the two deities, the Aśvins, [be] this!
O golden-winged one, you are gold... O you who fly through the sky, svāhā! This is for the golden-winged one.
O Dhanvantari, with the bow... may we conquer; Svāhā! This [is] for Dhanvantari.
I release him from Indra and Agni... for them, svāhā! To Indra and Agni, this [offering].
Anger is the deity;
may [the offering] mixed with... go forth, svāhā! This is for the fruit of the enemy.
The Viśākhā constellation is far from this... svāhā! This is for Indra and Agni.
O Conqueror of Death, O Three-eyed One... svāhā to Death, svāhā; this is for the Conqueror of Death.
I invoke here Śrī, who has the fragrance as her door, who is invincible, who is ever-nourishing and bestows prosperity, the sovereign of all beings— Śrī, Svāhā! This is for Śrī.

We invoke Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the bearer of oblations, the subduer of adversaries, the slayer of Rākṣasas, victorious in battles, radiant, shining, and the breaker of forts. O Agni, make this well-offered; accept the oblation. Overcome all hostile armies of the gods. Pointing out a wide path for us, shine forth; bestow upon us a long life full of light. Svāhā! This is for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.

He offers the *jaya*, *abhyātāna*, *āpya*, *bhṛt*, *prājāpatya*, the *ṛks* recited separately, and the *sauviṣṭakṛtī* oblations. Having touched the fuel-stick (*samidh*), the cord used for binding the sacrificial fuel (*idhma-sannahanī*), and water, he throws them into the fire with the formula: "To Rudra, the wanderer, this [is offered]. Having touched water, one who desires prosperity for the sake of the success of the ritual shall perform the *jaya* and other oblations. The first *āghāra* libation occurs after the principal oblation (*pradhānāhuti*). Whatever is to be offered—all that is stated by Kapardin in the *Sruva* [text]—constitutes the mouth of the fire (*agnimukha*).
Hariḥ Oṃ—He offers the other [portion] with the sruva-ladle.

*Śrī cittañca svāhā*—this is for *citta*. *Oṃ cittiśca svāhā*—this is for *citti*. *Ākūtañca svāhā*—this is for *ākūta*. *Ākūtiśca svāhā*—this is for *ākūti*. *Vijñātañca svāhā*—this is for *vijñāta*. *Vijñānañca svāhā*—this is for *vijñāna*.
*Manas* and *svāhā*—this is for *manas*. *Śakvarī*s and *svāhā*—this is for the two *śakvarī*s.
*Darśa* and *svāhā*—this is for *darśa*. *Pūrṇamāsa* and *svāhā*—this is for *pūrṇamāsa*.
Bṛhacchvasvāhe—by means of the Bṛhat, this.

To the Rathantara, Svāhā! To the Rathantara, this [offering]. Prajāpati gave the victories to Indra, the bull, the fierce one in the battles; all the people bowed down before him; he became the fierce, victorious, and worthy of oblation, Svāhā! To Prajāpati, this [offering].

Agni, the lord of beings, may he protect me in this sacred word (*brahman*), in this clan, in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this rite, and in this invocation of the gods; *svāhā*! To Agni, the lord of beings, [belongs] this [offering].

Indra, the sovereign lord of the eldest, may he prosper me in this sacred word (brahman), in this constellation, in this month, in this priestly office, in this rite, and in this invocation of the gods; Svāhā! To Indra, the sovereign lord of the eldest, [be] this [offering].

Yama is the lord of the earth; may he protect me in this Brahman-hood, in this Kṣatriya-hood, in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this rite, and in this invocation of the gods—svāhā! To Yama, the lord of the earth, [belongs] this.

Vāyu is the lord of the intermediate space. May he protect me in this Brahman-hood, in this Kṣatra-hood, in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, and in this divine oblation. Svāhā! To Vāyu, the lord of the intermediate space, [be] this.

Sūrya is the lord of heaven; may he protect me. I am a Brahmin, I am a Kṣatriya. In this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, in this offering to the gods—svāhā! To Sūrya, the lord of heaven, [be] this.

Candramas, the lord of the Nakṣatras, has bestowed prosperity upon me; I am a Brahmin, I am a Kṣatriya. May it be so in this blessing, in this priestly office, in this work, and in this offering to the gods. Svāhā! This is for Candramas, the lord of the Nakṣatras.

Bṛhaspati is the lord of the sacred word (*brahman*); may he protect me. I am the sacred word; I am the kṣatra. In this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, in this offering to the gods—svāhā! To Bṛhaspati, the lord of the sacred word, [I offer] this.

Mitra is the lord of truths; I am the equalizer, I am the Brahmin, I am the Kṣatriya, I am in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, in this offering to the gods—svāhā! To Mitra, the lord of truths, [be] this.

Varuṇa, lord of the waters, may you favor me; I am a Brahmin, I am a Kṣatriya. In this blessing, in this priestly office, in this ritual act, in this oblation to the gods—svāhā! To Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, [belongs] this.

The ocean is the overlord of rivers; I am equal to the Brahman, I am equal to the Kṣatra. In this blessing, in this office of domestic priest, in this work, in this offering to the gods—svāhā! To the ocean, the overlord of rivers, [be] this.

The Lord of universal sovereignties, may He protect me; in this assembly, in this sacred formulation, in this [status of] Brahmin, in this [status of] Kṣatriya, in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, in this divine oblation—Svāhā! To the Lord of universal sovereignties, to Agni, be this offering.

May Soma, the lord of plants, grant me prosperity in this [vocation], in this [assembly], in this [Brahman-hood], in this [Kshatriya-hood], in this [blessing], in this [priestly office], in this [act], and in this [offering to the gods]—svāhā! To Soma, the lord of plants, [be] this [offering].

Savitṛ is the overlord of instigations. I am a Brahmin, I am a Kṣatriya; may he lead me in this blessing, in this office of domestic priest, in this rite, in this offering to the gods—svāhā! This [is for] Savitṛ, the overlord of instigations.

Rudra, the lord of cattle, has protected me in this Brahman-hood, in this Kshatriya-hood, in this blessing, in this office of domestic priest, in this work, and in this offering to the gods; Svāhā! This [is for] Rudra, the lord of cattle.

Having touched it close by: "Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of forms, has made me prosper in this Brahman-hood, in this Kṣatra, in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, in this divine oblation, Svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of forms, [this]."

O Maruts, lords of the hosts, protect me; may you favor me in this [work], in this assembly, in this sacred word (*brahman*), in this princely power (*kṣatra*), in this blessing, in this leadership, in this ritual action, and in this divine oblation, *svāhā*! To the Maruts, the lords of the hosts, [be] this!

O fathers, grandfathers, great-grandfathers, and those further back, who have spread through the generations—protect us here! In this sacred word (*brahman*), in this governance (*kṣatra*), in this blessing (*āśis*), in this priesthood (*purodhā*), in this action (*karman*), and in this oblation to the gods (*devahūti*)—*svāhā*! This [is for] the gods, beginning with the fathers.
And if his father is still living.

O Grandfathers, who have extended through the lineages, protect us here. In this sacred word (*brahman*), in this protection, in this blessing, in this priesthood, in this work, and in this offering to the gods, *svāhā*—to the Grandfathers, the excellent ones, the great ones, this [is offered].
If they are the paternal grandfathers.

O Fathers who have passed away, protect us here; in this sacred word (*brahman*), in this power (*kṣatra*), in this blessing (*āśis*), in this priestly office (*purodhā*), in this work (*karman*), and in this offering to the gods (*devahūti*), [protect us].
*Svāhā*! This is for the remote ancestors.
While his father and grandfather are living, the *janana* (birth) rite must be performed for the son. Having touched water.

Agni, the Gandharva, who is the upholder of Truth and whose abode is Truth, has the Oṣadhīs (plants) as his Apsarases, named Ūrj (Strength). May they protect this spiritual power and this ruling power; may they protect this spiritual power and this ruling power. To him, Svāhā! To Agni, the Gandharva, the upholder of Truth and whose abode is Truth—this [is for him]. To them, Svāhā! To the Oṣadhīs, the Ūrjs—this [is for them].
The Gāndharva Viśvasāman, accompanied by the Marīcis as his Apsarases and the Āyus as his name—may he protect this priesthood and nobility; may he protect this priesthood and nobility. To him, Svāhā!
To the Gāndharva Viśvasāman, the Sun, this [offering]. To them, Svāhā! To the Marīcis, the Apsarases, and the Āyus, this [offering].

Suṣumna, the sun-rayed, the moon, the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Nakṣatras, named Bekuras. May they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra; may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, Svāhā! To Suṣumna, the sun-rayed, the moon, the Gandharva—this [be offered]. To them, Svāhā! To the Nakṣatras, the Apsarases, the Bekuras—this [be offered].

Bhujyu Suparṇa, the Gandharva, whose Apsarases are the Dakṣiṇās—may he protect this Brahman and Kṣatra; may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, Svāhā! To Bhujyu Suparṇa, the Gandharva, [this offering]. To them, Svāhā! To the Dakṣiṇās, the Apsarases, [this offering]. To them, [this offering].

Prajāpati Viśvakarman, whose vehicle is the mind, is the Gandharva; the Ṛc and Sāman verses are his Apsarases, and the fires are his Vānas. May he protect this Brahman and Kṣatra; may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, svāhā! To Prajāpati Viśvakarman, the Mind-Gandharva, this [offering]. To them, svāhā! To the Ṛc and Sāman Apsarases and the Fires, this [offering].

The Gandharva Viśvavyacas, the son of Iṣira, with the Apsarases Vāta and Mudā; and the Gandharva Ṛtāṣāṭ, the son of Ṛta, with Agni—may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To them, Svāhā! To Agni, the Gandharva, the conqueror of strength, whose abode is Truth—this [offering]!
May the Oṣadhī Apsarases named Ṛjūnas protect this Brahman and Kṣatra; to them, Svāhā! To the Oṣadhī Apsarases, to the Ūrjas, [be] this!
In this very [mantra], some northerners and southerners recite: "nāmasa idam svāhā."
To the vigorous, all-pervading Gandharva Vāta, this [offering]; Svāhā! To these Apsarases, the Waters, the Joyful Ones, this [offering].
O Lord of the World, whose dwellings are both above and here below, grant us wealth, prosperity, abundance, and well-being throughout the year; Svāhā! This is for the Lord of the World.

Parameṣṭhin is the overlord, Mṛtyu the Gandharva; his [consorts] are the Apsarases named Viśvabhuj. May he protect this priesthood and nobility; may they protect this priesthood and nobility. To him, svāhā! To Parameṣṭhin the overlord, to Mṛtyu, to the Gandharva Mṛtyu—this [offering]. To them, svāhā!—to the Apsarases Niśvas, to Bhū—this [offering].

Sukṣiti, Subhūti, Bhadrakṛt, Suvarvat, Parjanya the Gandharva—may his Apsaras, named Ruc, protect this Brahman and Kṣatra; may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, Svāhā! To Sukṣiti, to Subhūti, to Bhadrakṛt, to Suvarvat, to Parjanya the Gandharva—this [is offered] to them, Svāhā! To the Apsaras, the lightnings, the nourishments—this [is offered].

Far-darting Mṛḍaya, Mṛtyu, the Gandharva—his offspring are the fearful Apsarases; may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra, may they protect this Brahman and Kṣatra! To him, Svāhā! To the far-darting, to Mṛḍaya, to Mṛtyu, to the Gandharva—Svāhā to this! To his offspring, to the Apsarases, to the fearful ones—Svāhā to this!

To Cāru, the Gandharva who desires the wretched, and to his Apsarases, Śocayantī—svāhā! To Cāru, the Gandharva who desires the wretched, and to these Apsarases, Śocayantīs—this [is for them] svāhā! To the Apsarases, the Śocayantīs, this [is for them] svāhā!
O Lord of the world, for this Brahman, [I offer] great protection and that which is vast; svāhā! O Lord of the world, this is for the Brahman.
Meditating upon Prajāpati with the mind.
O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all created beings. Whatever we offer to you with our desire, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches—svāhā! This is for Prajāpati.
Bhūḥ svāhā—this is for Agni. Bhuvaḥ svāhā—this is for Vāyu.
Svāhā! To Sūrya, this [offering].
Whatever I have overdone in this rite, or whatever I have done here deficiently—may Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, the wise one, make all that well-sacrificed and well-offered. Svāhā! This is for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.

Having removed the *śamyā* pegs and having cast away the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*), while casting away the other two, he hides the tip of the northern stick among the embers. Having consecrated the enclosing-sticks with a mantra, he throws down two *āghāra*-fuel sticks, dedicating them to all the gods.

He offers with the residue: "To all the gods who have a share in the residue, this [is offered]. In this primary rite, for the purpose of expiation for the omission or transposition of other rites, he recites: "With songs... and so forth.
This is for the purpose of expiation in the event of a lapse in the restraint of speech.

I shall offer oblations with these Vyahṛtis—*viṣṇu triyambakam*, for the purpose of expiating the ignorance of the officiating priests; *yadvidvāṃsaḥ*, for the purpose of expiating defects such as spilling [the offering]; *māskāndoḥ*, for the purpose of expiating defects involving Indra and others; *yanma ātmanaḥ*, for the purpose of removing all defects arising from fear and the like; *punaragniśca kṣuḥ*, for the purpose of expiating the injury to the fire; and *pinastvādityāḥ*, for the purpose of general expiation—with these mantras, namely *bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ*. I shall offer the oblations.
Oṃ! Whatever has been performed in the sacrifice that was not known or was known [only partially]—O Agni, make this well-prepared for him; you indeed know how it truly is—svāhā! This is for Agni.
The sacrifice is commensurate with the Person; the sacrifice is commensurate with the Person. O Agni, ordain this for him; you indeed know how it should be done. Svāhā!—this is for Agni.

When the wise mortals, striving for skill, have meditated upon you as the one who eats the mind at the sacrifice, then Agni, the Hotṛ, knowing the ritual, the most excellent sacrificer among the gods, shall sacrifice according to the seasons. Svāhā! To Agni belongs this [offering].

O Agni, you who know, dispel for us the wrath of the god Varuṇa; as the best sacrificer, the most excellent bearer of oblations, and the radiant one, utterly drive away from us all hatreds and sins. This [offering] is for Agni and Varuṇa.

O Agni, be our protector; be near us, most close to us at this dawn. Granting release from consumption, O Varuṇa, deliver us; be a source of great joy and well-being for us, Svāhā! This [is] for Agni and Varuṇa.
With these songs, whatever is deficient in us, may you fill up;

increasing, O possessor of bay horses, as you grant to the singers the breaking open of great enclosures, may we be those who receive the greatest share of your bounty—svāhā! This [is for] Indra, the lord of the bay horses.
Here Viṣṇu strode forth; he established his foot in three places. His step is encompassed in the highest heaven—svāhā! This is for Śrī Mahāviṣṇu.
We worship the three-eyed one, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity. May I be freed from death, as a cucumber from its stalk, and attain immortality. Svāhā! This [is for] Tryambaka.

Whatever the priests do, whether they are learned or unlearned, or whether they act out of ignorance—may Agni and the goddess Śraddhā release me from that sin, svāhā! To Agni and the goddess Śraddhā, this [offering]. The heaven has not stumbled, nor the earth; the young bull has not stumbled. From what has not stumbled, these [beings] are born; from what has not stumbled, the bull procreates. May I procreate from what has not stumbled, svāhā! To the deities beginning with Skanna, this [offering].
Whatever breach there was of my self, Agni Jātavedas, the far-seeing, has restored that; svāhā!—this is for the deities beginning with Minda.
Again may Agni give me sight, again Indra and Bṛhaspati; again may the Aśvins, O ye two physicians, bestow sight upon my eyes, svāhā!—this is for Agni, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and the Aśvins.

Again may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle you; again may the Brahmins, the bestowers of wealth, [kindle you] with sacrifices. May you increase us with clarified butter; may the desires of the sacrificer come true—Svāhā! This [is for] Agni, the bestower of wealth.
I shall perform the full expiation (*sarva-prāyaścitta*), which consists of half of the expiation for all possible transgressions of the ritual injunctions that have been committed.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā; this is for Prajāpati. Svāhā to Śrī Viṣṇu; this is for Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self.
Having taken twelve portions and filled the ladle with clarified butter.

*Oṃ! Seven are your fuel-sticks, O Agni; seven your tongues, seven your seers, and seven your dear oblations. Fill these seven wombs with this full-offering; bathe yourself in the clarified butter, Svāhā!* "To Agni, the seven-fold priest, [this offering]. He offers this final full-oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Indeed, the full-oblation is everything; he thereby obtains everything. This final full-oblation is indeed the foundation; he thus finds firm support in it. He offers the stream of wealth (*vasordhārā*). This is offered as the "stream of wealth"; it is the stream of clarified butter that nourishes him in yonder world and establishes him there. He offers with clarified butter.

Clarified butter is brilliance, and wives are brilliance; verily, he bestows brilliance upon him, and through brilliance he wins brilliance. Wives are indeed a stream of prosperity; verily, he wins desires themselves.
May the Pūrṇāhuti be a moment of auspiciousness; may they grant their approval.
May there be auspicious moments.
O Āditi, you have stood upon this path; O Anumati, you have stood upon this path; O Sarasvatī, you have stood upon this path; O God Savitṛ, you have impelled [us]; O Vraṇītā, for our own protection.

May you be good to me; may everything be mine; you are all, may everything be mine; you are full, may I be full; you are imperishable, do not perish for me. With that purifier of yours with which they always purify themselves, with that thousand-streamed one, may you purify my sin. The purifier belonging to Prajāpati, golden and having a hundred openings—with that, we who know Brahman purify the purified Brahman. May Indra purify us with his guidance, Soma with well-being, Varuṇa with his straight path, King Yama with his destroyers of evil, and Jātavedas with his life-sustaining power.
May the gods and the officiating priests purify me in the eastern direction; may the months and the ancestors purify me in the southern direction.

May the houses and cattle purify themselves in the western direction; may the waters, the plants, and the trees purify themselves in the northern direction; may the sacrifice, the year, and the lord of the sacrifice purify themselves in the upward direction.

"I send you forth to the ocean; go back to your own source. May I remain unbroken in my progeny; let not my vital fluid flow away. He takes the full vessel into his cupped hands: "Verily, he bestows seed and progeny upon her, for by progeny a human being is made full. He releases his mouth. Having assumed the form of the *āvabṛdha* (the one who has pushed down), he stands up, holding the uncrushed grain upon his head.
May there be peace; may there be nourishment; may there be abundance of wealth and grain; may there be success in all undertakings; may the Blessed Lord Vāstoṣpati be pleased.

One should spread the sacrificial grass starting from the east and release it at the north. "I give a boon to Brahman. "I remove the grasses from the fire. He becomes radiant, glorious, and endowed with the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcas*).
At the conclusion of the *homa*, [one says]: "Obeisance to the illustrious Yajñapuruṣa; I offer the worship consisting of the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*), beginning with meditation (*dhyāna*)."
O Havyavāhana, grant me well-being, faith, intelligence, fame, wisdom, learning, discernment, prosperity, strength, longevity, splendor, and health.

I salute that Consumer of Oblations (Hutāśana), by whose remembrance and name alone the acts of austerity, fire-offerings, and rituals reach completion even when deficient; O God, may whatever has been offered by me become perfectly complete for you.
O Blessed One, through this offering of nine oblations, may You, the Lord of Sacrifice, who are the self of all and all things, be pleased.
Salutation to the nine planetary deities, beginning with Āditya, who reside in the pavilion. Salutation to the eight guardian deities of the directions, beginning with Indra.
I shall perform worship once again.

I hold the parasol; I fan with the chowries; I present the dance; I cause the song to be heard; I cause the instrumental music to resound; I cause [the deity] to be mounted upon a palanquin; I cause [the deity] to be mounted upon horses; I cause [the deity] to be mounted upon elephants; I offer all royal services, divine services, services of devotion, and worship.
By this worship, may the nine planets beginning with Āditya and the eight guardians of the directions beginning with Indra be well-pleased, highly gratified, and granters of boons.

By means of sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the Sacrifice; those were the first established ordinances. They attained the heights of heaven, those great ones, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide.
I install the deities residing in the pavilion in their respective places.

Oṃ! Bṛhatsāman, the sustainer of the kṣatra, the great, the virile—O you who are adorned with the Triṣṭubh meter, the mighty hero! With the fifteen-fold Stoma and with Vāta, the purifier, protect this center.
Come together and behold this most auspicious bride; having bestowed upon her good fortune, depart from here.
Oṃ! Agni, you who know all things, for the sake of supporting us—supporting us—ward off from us all sins that lead astray; we shall offer to you the most abundant speech of homage.

Bring forth the oblation and the prayer for Agni, the pure, radiant light; he who, having been born among both divine and human races, moves with wisdom toward all things. Toward Agni proceed the songs and prayers, O God, as they seek wealth under his guidance—he who is fair to behold, of beautiful countenance, self-luminous, the bearer of oblations, and the messenger of mankind. O Agni, drive away from us those who are hostile; let the people who lack the protection of fire fall into misfortune. Grant us again prosperity, O Gods, so that we may dwell upon the earth with all [the gods].

O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, with these [hymns] do thou, the protector, carry us across all difficulties by means of thy auspicious blessings—may the city and the broad, expansive earth be a refuge for Kāya and Tanaya, who seek glory.
The ladle, being stirred by the mind, is led straight toward the oblation; moving to the right, the swift and vigorous one goes forward, bearing the ghee-dripping offering for Agni.

Salutations to you, the Lord of the Household; salutations to you, the Southern Fire (Dakṣiṇāgni); salutations to the Āhavanīya fire and to the Great Altar (Mahāvedi). Salutations again and again to the Great Altar, who is the embodiment of the Brahman and the ritual action accomplished through the two sections (Kāṇḍas). Salutations again and again to the Lord of Sacrifice, who consists of both heaven and the beyond-heaven, and who is the embodiment of the Brahman and the ritual action accomplished through the two sections. O Acyuta, Govinda, Mādhava, Ananta, Keśava, Lord of Sacrifice!

O Kṛṣṇa, O Viṣṇu, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Vāsudeva, salutations to you! Salutations to you for one time; salutations to you for two times; salutations to you for three times; salutations to you for four times; salutations to you five times; salutations to you ten times; salutations to you a hundred times; salutations to you a thousand times! Homage be to you; do not harm me. I am on the far side; I am on this side. By means of light, I have dispelled the darkness. That which is the intermediate space—that has become my father. I have beheld the sun from both sides. May I become the most excellent among my equals.

Oṃ! May we be free from debt in this world, free from debt in the next, and free from debt in the third world; may we discharge our debts on all paths—those leading to the gods and those leading to the ancestors.

"If, while performing a ritual action, it should fall away due to negligence, it becomes complete through the mere remembrance of Viṣṇu"—such is the Smṛti. One should therefore perform the remembrance of Viṣṇu.

Thus end the rites beginning with *jayā*. Now, the "Beholding of the Face" (*mukhāvalokanam*): having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). In this manner—for the sake of pleasing the Supreme Lord, by means of removing all calamities such as the forbidden lunar days, weekdays, and asterisms for a boy born under the first quarter of the asterism Uttarā, and intending to perform the rite called the "Sacrifice to the Planets" (*grahamakhākhya*) preceded by the Beholding of the Face—I shall, as a preliminary part thereof, at the very outset, together with great men and my kinsmen, recite the benediction (*svasti*) for the sake of purification, prosperity, pacification, and exaltation.
I shall perform the recitation for the declaration of an auspicious day.

Having first performed the worship of the Lord of the Gaṇas for them, and having had the declaration of an auspicious day (*puṇyāha*) recited, one should perform the planetary sacrifice (*grahamakhā*) preceded by the ritual of beholding their faces (*mukhāvalokana*).

Oṃ. He became the counterpart of every form; that form of his was for the purpose of being seen. Indra moves in many forms through his powers of illusion; for his bay steeds, a hundred and ten, are yoked.
May the moment of beholding your face be a most auspicious moment.

Having thus performed the salutation of the faces and completed the worship of the planets according to the previously mentioned procedure, one should perform the respective fire-offerings (*homa*), gifts (*dāna*), and so forth, in accordance with the rules.

In the case of merely beholding the face, one should perform the worship of Gaṇādhipati and the recitation of the Puṇyāha formula after having beheld the face—this is the procedure for beholding the face. Having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa): "I shall perform the offering of ghee that has been gazed upon."
Having honored the Brahmin who accepts [the gift], he should give him the examined clarified butter along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and betel.
"Whatever misfortune and whatever obesity is present throughout all the limbs—pacify all that, O worthy one, and increase prosperity and nourishment"—with these words, he should offer it.

Thus ends the examination of the faces. Now begins the section on the *pravara* lineages of Bodhāyana—[the lineage of] Bodhāyana. "As long as there is only one sage who recurs in the *pravara*s, so long is there a commonality of *gotra*; this is the case except for the *Aṅgirasa*s and the *Bhṛgu*s. (Mādhavīya, Smṛtyantara). "In the case of the five [groups], there is no marriage if there is a commonality among three; in the case of the three, it is forbidden if there is a commonality among two. This applies to the *Bhṛgu* and *Aṅgiras* groups; in the remaining [groups], even a single common [sage] prohibits marriage. (Nirṇayasindhu). The meaning of its half-verse is: "In the remaining *gotra*s, even a single common *pravara* shall prohibit marriage."

Baudhāyana also, taking Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras as the limit—stating that when there is a meeting of two *ṛṣis*, those with three *ṛṣis* may not intermarry; when there is a meeting of three *ṛṣis*, those with five *ṛṣis* may not intermarry—and regarding the groups of Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, among the Jamadagnis, Gautamas, and Bharadvājas, there is no marriage even if there is identity in only one *pravara*, whereas for others, there is no marriage if there is non-identity [in the *pravara*] due to being of the same *gotra*.

Baudhāyana states: "The lineages (gotras) are indeed in the thousands, millions, and billions; however, there are only forty-nine of them, as determined by the vision of the ancestral sages (pravaras). In the *Nirṇayasindhu*: "There are seven Bhṛgu groups—the Vatsas, Vidas, Ārṣṇiṣeṇas, Yāskas, Mitrayus, Vaiṇyas, and Śunakas. Because their pravaras are identical, they must all avoid intermarrying with one another, even though they belong to different sub-groups. Then, regarding the Aṅgirases: "They are threefold: the Gautamas, the Bharadvājas, and the pure Aṅgirases."

Herein are the ten Gautamas: the Āyāsyas, Śaradvantas, Komaṇḍas, Dīrghatamasas, Auśanasas, Kāreṇupāleyas, Rāhūgaṇas, Somarājakas, Vāmadevas, and Bṛhadukthas. Now the Bharadvājas, who are fourfold: the Bharadvājas, Gargas, Ṛkṣas, and Kavayas. Now the exclusive Aṅgirasas: the Haritas, Aṅgirasas, Kaṇvas, Rathītaras, Mudgalas, and Viṣṇuvṛddhas, as well as the Kutsas.

The Ātreyas: the Ātreyas, the Vādṛtakas, the Gaviṣṭaras, and the Mudgalas. Then the Viśvāmitras: the Teḍas, the Kulikas, the Lauhītas, the Kākṣakas, the Kāmakāyanas, the Katas, the Dhanañjayas, the Aghamarṣaṇas, the Pūrāṇas, and the Indrakauśikas. Then the Kaśyapas: they are five—the Nidruvas, the Kaśyapas, the Śāṇḍilas, the Rekhās, and the Laugākṣayas. Then the Vasiṣṭhas: they are five—the Vāsiṣṭhas, the Kuṇḍinas, the Upamanyus, the Parāśaras, and the Jātūkarṇas.

Now, the Āgastyas—those four groups being the Idmavāhas, Sāṃbhavāhas, Somavāhas, and Yajñavāhas. Next, the Dvigotras—the Śauṅgas, Śaiśiriṇas, Kātyas, and Akṣīlas; their marriages are with the Bhṛgus and the Viśvāmitras. Likewise, according to the *Prayogapārijāta*, there is no marriage for the Kapilas, Katas, Saṃkṛtis, Pūtimāṣas, and others with those within their own group, nor with the Vasiṣṭhas, Śauṅgas, Śaiśiras, Laugākṣis, or even the Kaśyapas.

By day they are Vasiṣṭhas, by night they are Kaśyapas; among them, marriage occurs between the Vasiṣṭhas and the Kaśyapas. According to the *Prayogapārijāta*, there is no marriage between Devarāta and the descendants of Jamadagni or the Viśvāmitras. There is one Devarāta who is an Aṅgirasa, and another Devarāta who is a Bhārgava; there is no marriage between the Bhārgava Devarāta and Jamadagni’s lineage. For the Dhananjayas, there is no marriage with the Viśvāmitras or the Atris. For the Jātukarṇyas, there is no marriage with the Vasiṣṭhas or the Atris.

There is no marriage between those of the same *gotra* for both the giver and the receiver of a daughter. For Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas, there is no marriage with one who knows the family priest (*purohita*) or the lineage of cows (*gojña*). For all classes, there is no marriage within one's own group (*svagaṇa*). Although a marriage between the Kaṇva and Bharadvāja lineages is mentioned in the *Pariśiṣṭa* of the Bahvṛcas, it is nonetheless prohibited in works such as the *Smṛtyarthasāra*. In all cases, the settled rule is to be understood according to the local customs and family traditions of the respective regions.
Bharadvāja, Kavi, Garga, and Raukṣāyaṇa—these four also did not intermarry because they shared the same lineage within the Bharadvāja gotra.
The ancestral lineages (*gotra-pravaras*) are as follows: in the *bhṛgu* group, for the *vatsas*, they are Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya;
or Bhārgava, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya—this constitutes the triple-lineage (*trārṣeya*).
The triple-lineage (ārṣeya) is Bhārgava-Cyāvāna-Āpnavāna.
[The individual names are] Vidāna, Bhāra, Vyāna, Āpnavāna, Jāhuṣa, and Vaidadaśvi.
[The lineage is] Bhārgava-Urvajā-Agniveśya. These two are designated as Jāmadagnya.
Āṣṇīrṣeṇa, Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnavāna, Āṣṇīrṣeṇa, and Anūpa—these are the Bhārgava-Āṣṇīrṣeṇa-Anūpas. There is no intermarriage among these.
Among the Vātsyas, [the lineage is] Bhārgava, Cyāvana, and Āpnavāna.

For the descendants of Vatsa and Purohita: Bhārgava, Āpacyutana, Āpnavāna, Vātsa, and Pauraudhana; for those born of Bhejavana and Mathita: Bhārgava, Cyāvāśva, Āpnavāna, Bhaijavāna, and Māthita—among these there is no intermarriage.
For the Āyāsya-kāṇvas: Bhārgava, Vaitahavya, and Sāvedasa.
The lineage of the Mitrayus is: Bhārgava, Vādryaśva, and Divodāsa;
or Bhārgava, Cyavana, and Divodāsa;
or simply Vādryaśva alone.
For the Vainyas— these [rites] belong to Bhārgava, Vainya, and Pārtha.
For the Śunakas—
it is either Śunaka or Gārtsamada.
For those of the Bhṛgu lineage: *bhārgava-gārtsamada-aiti* is for one who has two ancestors; *bhārgava-śaunahotra-gārtsamada* is [for one with three];
for those of the Veda and Viśvajyotis lineages: *bhārgava-veda-vaiśvajyotiṣa*.

For the Śāṭhara-Māṭharas— their *pravara* being Bhārgava-Śāṭhakara-Māṭhara— there is no marriage within their own group due to the identity of their *pravara*, but there is marriage with all others. For the Ayaska, Mitrāyuvā, Vaiśya, and Śunaka lineages,
there is no marriage within their own group due to the identity of their *pravara*, but there is marriage with all others.
Now, among the groups of Aṅgirases, there are ten starting with Gautama:
for those of the Āyāsya lineage—Āṅgirasa, Ayāsya, and Gautama;
for those of the Śāradvata lineage—Āṅgirasa, Gautama, and Śāradvata.
For the Kaumaṇḍas: Āṅgirasa, Audadhyaka, Kākṣīvanta, Gautama, and Kaumaṇḍa.
For the Āyasyas: Āṅgirasa, Āyāsya, Auśija, Gautama, and Kākṣīvat.
For the [others]: Āṅgirasa, Auchatya, Gautama, Auśija, and Kākṣīvat.
For the Āṅgirasas of the Auśija-Kākṣivats: *Āṅgirasa, Aucathya, Kākṣīvata, Gautama, Dairghatamasa*. For the Dīrghatamasas: *Āṅgirasa, Aucathyaka, Kākṣīvata, Gautama, Dairghatamasa*.
For the Auśanasas: *Āṅgirasa, Gautama, Kārṣṇapaulya*.
Of the Kāreṇupālas: "O descendant of Aṅgiras, Gautama, Kāreṇupāla!
Of the Rahūgaṇas: "O descendant of Aṅgiras, Gautama, Somarājaka! Of the Somarājakas: "O descendant of Aṅgiras, Gautama, Somarājaka!"
For the Vāmadevas: Āṅgirasa, Vāmadeva, Gautama.
For the Bṛhadukthas: Āṅgirasa, Bārhaduktha, Gautama;
or Āṅgirasa, Vāmadeva, Bārhaduktha.
For those of the Ucathya lineage: Āṅgirasa, Aucathya, Gautama. For those of the Auśija lineage: Āṅgirasa, Auśija, Kākṣīvata.
[Or alternatively: Āṅgirasa, Āyāsya, Auśija, Gautama, Kākṣīvata.

Regarding the Raghuvansas—some say they are Āṅgīrasa, Rāghava, and Gautama. There is no mutual marriage among all those belonging to the Gautama lineage. Within the Āṅgirasagaṇa, there are four Bharadvājas;
for the Bharadvājas, [the gotras are] Āṅgīrasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja.
Of the Gargas: Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Gārgya, and Śainya;
or Āṅgirasa, Śainya, and Gārgya;
or Bhāradvāja, Gārgya, and Śainya.
For the Gargabhodas: Āṅgirasa, Taittirīka, and Pibhuva.
For the Ṛkṣas and the Kapis: Āṅgirasa, Bārhasvatya, Bharadvāja, Vāndana, and Mātavacasa;
[or] Āṅgirasa, Vāndana, and Mātavacasa.
For the Kapilas: Āṅgirasa, Āmahīyava, Ṛkṣa, Yavasa. For the Ātmabhūs: Āṅgirasa, Bhāradvāja, Bārhaspatya, Mantravara, Ātmabhū.
Now, the Kevalāṅgirasas.
Of the Haritas—Āṅgirasa, Ambarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva; of the Māndhātṛs—Ambarīṣa and Yauvanāśva;
of the Kutsas—Āṅgirasa, Māndhātṛ, and Kutsa.
For the Kaṇvas: Āṅgirasa, Ājamīḍhaka, and Āṅgyeti.
For the Āṅgirasas: Ghoraka and Kāṇva.
For the Rathītaras: Āṅgirasa, Vairūpa, and Rāthītara.
For the Āṅgirasas:
either *Vairūpa-pārṣadaśva* or *Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra-pārṣadaśva-vairūpa*.
For the Maudgalas: *Āṅgirasa-bhārmyaśva-maudgalya*.
Tārkṣyabhārmyaśva Maudgalya;
Āṅgīrasa Tārkṣya Maudgalya. For the Viṣṇuvṛddhas: Āṅgīrasa Paurukutsatraasadasya.
For these [families], marriage takes place with all [others] except for their own *gaṇa*. However, it does not take place between the Haris and the Kutsas. Now, within the Āṅgirasa and Atri *gaṇas*:
For the Ātreyas: Ātreya, Arcanānasa, and Śyāvāśva. For the Vādbhutakas: Ātreya, Arcanānasa, and Vādbhutaka. For the Dhanañjayas: Ātreya, Arcanānasa, and Dhānañjaya.
For the Gaviṣṭharas—Ātreya Ārcanānasa [is the seer] of the Gaviṣṭhara hymns;
Ātreya Gaviṣṭhara Paurvātithi [is the seer].
For the Mudgalas—Ātreya Ārcanānasa Paurvātithi [is the seer].
Of the Vāmarathyas, the Sumaṅgalas, and the Baijavāsas, [the gotra] is Ātreya, Arcanānasa, and Atidhi.
Or, for the Ātreyas and Arcanānasas, it is Gaviṣṭhira.
For the Sumaṅgalas, some say it is Atri, Sumaṅgala, and Śyāvāśva.

The lineage of Atri’s daughters’ sons consists of the Ātreyas, Vāmarathyas, and Pautrikas; there is intermarriage among all ten of these branches of the Atris. The lineage of the Kuśikas consists of the Viśvāmitras, Devarātas, and Saudalas.
The lineage of the Lauhitas consists of the Viśvāmitras, Aṣṭakas, and Lauhitas.
For the Vaiśvāmitras Mādhucchandasas, it is Vaiśvāmitra, Mādhucchandasa, and Aṣṭake-tiva;
or Vaiśvāmitra and Aṣṭaka.
For the Raukṣakas, it is Vaiśvāmitra, Gādhi, and Naraivaṇa.
For the Vaiśvāmitras of the Gādhi lineage, the *praśna* is "vaṇe. For the Vaiśvāmitras of the Raukṣaka lineage, the *praśna* is "vaṇe.
For the Kāmakāyanas—the Vaiśvāmitras of Devaśravas and Devātithi—the *sūtra* is "seti."
For the Ājāna hymns: Vaiśvāmitra Mādhucchandasa.
Or [the lineage] of Vaiśvāmitra is Āśmarathya Vādhūla.
For the Aghamarṣaṇa hymns: Vaiśvāmitra Āghamarṣaṇa Kauśika.
For the Pūraṇas: "Vaiśvāmitra, Pūraṇa" or "Vaiśvāmitra, Devarāta, Pūraṇa. For the Indrakauśikas: "Viśvāmitra, Indrakauśika."
For the Dhananjayas: Vaiśvāmitra, Mādhucchandasa, and Dhananjaya;
or alternatively, Vaiśvāmitra, Mādhucchandasa, and Āghamarṣaṇa.
For the Katis: Vaiśvāmitra, Kata, and Autkīla.
Of the Rauhiṇas: Vaiśvāmitra, Mādhucandana, and Rauhiṇa.
Of the Reṇus: Vaiśvāmitra, Gādhi, and Nairama. Of the Veṇus: Vaiśvāmitra, Gādhi, and Nairaṇava.
Of the Jahnus: Vaiśvāmitra, Śālaṅkāyana, and Kauśika. Of the Āśmaradhyas: Vaiśvāmitra, Āśmaradhya, and Vādhūla.
Of the Udaveṇus: Vaiśvāmitra, Gādhi, and Vaiṇava.
Seventeen [gotras] are mentioned by Bodhāyana; six by Āśvalāyana; and in the Matsya Purāṇa: "There is no intermarriage among these Viśvāmitras. Now, regarding the Kaśyapa group:
Of the Nidhruvas: Kāśyapa, Āvatsāra, and Naidhruva.
Of the Kaśyapas: Kāśyapa, Āvatsāra, and Asita. Of the Rebhas: Kāśyapa, Āvatsāra, and Raibhya.
For the Śāṇḍilas: Kāśyapa-Śāṇḍilya;
Kāśyapa-Devālā;
Kāśyapa-Asitā.
"Kāṇḍila, Asita Devala," or "Asita,
Devala," or "Devala, Asita."
Among these, the marriage of those named Kāśyapa is with the Kāśyapas; that of the Laugākṣis is with the Kāśyapas;
and that of the Vatsas is with the Ārṣṭiṣeṇas and the Vasiṣṭhas.
[The Vasiṣṭhas] are of two lineages: those of Kaśyapa and those of Vatsa-Asita.
These are the two ancestral clans. By day they are Vasiṣṭhas; by night they are Kaśyapas. There is no intermarriage between these Vasiṣṭhas and Kaśyapas.
Among the Vasiṣṭhas, [the sub-lineages are] Vāsiṣṭha, Indrapramada, and Ābharadvasu.
The Vāsiṣṭhas have only one [gotra]: Vāsiṣṭha.
Among the Kuṇḍinas—Vāsiṣṭha, Maitrāvaruṇa, and Kauṃjinya.
Among the Upamanyus—Vāsiṣṭha, Indrapramada, and Ābhāradvāja.
For the Vāsiṣṭhas: Vāsiṣṭha, Bhāradvāja, and Aindrapramada.
For the Parāśaras: Vāsiṣṭha, Śāktya, and Pārāśarya. For the Jātūkarṇyas: Vāsiṣṭha, Ātreya, and Jātūkarṇya.
There is no marriage among all the Vāsiṣṭhas.
However, for the Jātūkarṇyas, there is no marriage with the Vāsiṣṭhas or the Atris,
because of their shared dual gotra.
In the *Atharvaveda* lineage:
[the hymn] of Idhmavāha—[namely] "Of Agastya, of Dārbhyacyuta, of Idhmavāha. Or, "Of Agastya" alone.

For those who carry the Soma: "O Agastya, Dārdhya, Acyuta, Soma-vāha! For those who carry the Sāmbha: "O Agastya, Dārdhya, Acyuta, Sāmbha-ha! For those who carry the sacrifice: "O Agastya, Dārdhya, Acyuta, Yajña-vāha!"
For those carrying *sāra* wood: "O Agastya, Dārḍhya, Cyuta, Sāravāha! For those carrying *darbha* grass: "O Agastya, Dārḍhya, Cyuta, Darbhavāha!
For the Agastis: "O Agastya, Māhendra, Māyobhu!"
Of the Pūrṇamāsa [observances]: "The breaking of the fast on the full moon day of Āgastya.
Of the Himodaka [observances]: "The Himodaka [observance] of Āgastya and Haimarcis.
Of the Pāṇika [observances]: "The Pāṇika [observance] of Āgastya and Vaināyatas."
The marriage of all the Agastis is [permissible] with the Sāravāhas and others in certain cases;
that of the Śauṅgas and Śaiśirīs is [with those of the lineages]: Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Kātya, and Akṣīla;
or [alternatively]: Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Śauṅga, and Śaiśira.
Āṅgīrasa, Kātya, and Ākṣīla—
there is no marriage between these and the Bharadvājas or the Viśvāmitras.
For the Kapilas, the Katas, the Saṃkṛtis, the Pūtimāṣas, and so forth, [the gotra] is Āṅgīrasa-Gauravīta.
Regarding "Sāṃkṛtya":
[the term] "Sāṃkṛtya" is derived from Śāktya and Gaurīvita.
These [lineages] have no matrimonial alliance with the Vasiṣṭhas, Śauṅgaśaiśiras, or Laugākṣis who reside within their own respective groups, because of the unity of these three groups.
Regarding the Laugākṣis: some say there is marriage with the Vasiṣṭhas and the Kaśyapas;
others say there is marriage with the Devarātās, the Jāmadagnyas, and the Viśvāmitras. There are two types of Devarātas: one is a Jāmadagnya.
However, there is indeed an intermarriage between that Devarāta of the Āṅgirasa lineage and the son of Jamadagni—namely, the marriage of Devarāta Bhārgava with those of the Bhṛgu lineage.
There is no intermarriage between the Dhananjayas and the Viśvāmitras or the Atris.
And there is no intermarriage between the Jātūkarṇyas and the Vasiṣṭhas or the Atris.

In the *Smṛtyarthasāra*: "The Kapis, Gargas, Bhāradvājas, Mithis, Aurvas, and Aukṣāyaṇas—these twice-born men should not marry one another because they share the same lineage (*gotra*) and, in some cases, the same *pravara*."

In the *Nirṇayasindhu*: although this has been stated in the *Pravaramañjarī*, nevertheless, marriage does indeed take place between those belonging to the *Bhṛgu* and *Aṅgiras* groups. This is because, according to the *Bahvṛcapariśiṣṭa*, Bodhāyana prohibits [marriage] between the *Bhṛgu* and *Aṅgiras* groups due to their lack of common ancestry (*vyāvartitatvāt*). Furthermore, in the *Caturviṃśatimata*, by the statement of Bhṛgu, it is ordained that one must follow the local customs and family traditions inherited through successive generations. As for the authoritative statement governing all cases: "Among the five [groups], there is a commonality among three; since forty-nine of these have been seen as seers (*ṛṣi*), they constitute the *pravara*s."
There are thousands, millions, and hundreds of millions of lineages.
Bhṛgu, Jamadagni, Vītahavya, Gṛtsamada, Vādhyraśva,
Vainya, Jamadagni, Vītahāsya, Gṛtsamada, Vādhyraśva, and Vainya.
Vatsa, Āyaska, Śauna, Maitryava, Pārtha,
Śrīvatsa, Mauna, Cyavana, and Loka.
Āpnuvāna, Vādhūla, Aurva, Sāveda, and Sāvarṇi.
Jīvaṃti, Devarāta, and Īśāyana.
The hero Jābāli [is from] Hityavaṭa.
Maṇḍu Prācīnayogya Ārṣīṣeṇa.
The Ānūpakas, the Bhṛgus, the Vasiṣṭhas, the Tatās, Devarāta the descendant of Aṅgiras, the Agastyas, the Saṃkṛtis, and the Dhanañjayas.
The Atrayas, Śauṅgas, Pūtimāṣas, Jātukarṇyas, Viśvāmitras, Śaiśiriṇas, Laugākṣyas,
Kaśyapas, Kapilas, and Devarātas.
Atri, Viśvāmitra, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Āgastya;
Atri, Viśvāmitra, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Āgastya;
Atri, Viśvāmitra, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Āgastya.
Anenas, Devarāta, Repha, Indrapramada,
Ārḍhyacyuti, Śāvāśya, Manu, Raipha, Ābharadvasu, Idhmavāha, Vāmaradhya, Taṇṭu, Śāṇḍilya, and Saṃkṛti.
Gaviṣṭhara Aulava, Devala Kauṇḍinya, Dhanañjaya Vālava, Āsita Pūtimāṣa, Sumaṅgala Cakita, and Saṃkṛti Goravīta.
Atidhi, Ulūka, Pūtimāṣa, Parāśara, Bījavāpin, Yājñavalkya, Avatsāra, Maitrāvaruṇa,
Audava, Naidhruva, and Śakti.
Bṛhadagni, Upamanyu, Kulabīja, Śalila, and Devaśravas.
Babhru, Dhanañjaya, Lohita, Panasa, Śālaṅkāyana, and Dhūmra.
Pārītya Jaṭhara Kāmakāyana, Havyaka Kāmakāyana, and Sāṣava.
Pūraṇa, Sāṣāvā, Śālāvata, Śṛṅga,
Agnidevatya, and Kata.
Śraumati, Śaiśira, Kauśika, Aghamarṣaṇa, and Aṣṭaka.
Ajya Madhucchandas Gautama, Bharadvāja Kapi, Harita Kaṇva, Varūpa Maudgalya, and Viṣṇuvṛddha.

Gautama, Bharadvāja, Kapi, Harita, Kaṇva, Virūpa, Maudgalya, Viṣṇuvṛddha, Ayāsya, Kuk, Mahāt, Yavanāśva, Ajāmīḷha, Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra, Trakṣu, Paurukutsya, Autidhya, Agni, Akṣāyya, Māndhātṛ, Pṛṣadaśva, Bhrāmyaśva,
Trasadaśva, Vāmadeva, Śṛṅga, Śaṅkha, and Bādarāyaṇa.
Ṛkṣa, Bhīma, Sātyaki,
Vāndana, Virūpa, Bṛhaspati, and Gavi.
Sarva, Satyaki, Stamba, Āruṇi, and Kapi.
Mātāvacasa Gārgya.
Śainya:
Salutations to the venerable Gurus. Now begins the section on the *pravara* lineages according to Āpastamba.

We shall explain the *pravara* (the invocation of ancestors). "He chooses the *ārṣeya* (ancestral lineage), for [it serves] as a bond, and also for continuity," so it is known. One should not choose the *ārṣeya* by means of gods or men; rather, one should choose the *ārṣeya* by means of the *ṛṣis*, for it is known: "He proclaims the *ārṣeya*; for through the *ṛṣi*, the gods recognize the human being. It is known: "If one who is one thing chooses the *ārṣeya* of another, he takes away from him that which was desired and obtained by the *ṛṣi*. He chooses three *mantrakṛts* (makers of mantras); he chooses two.

"One chooses three; one should not choose four; one should not choose more than five"—thus it is known. "From here upwards the Adhvaryu chooses; from the *mut* onwards the Hotṛ"—thus it is known. "The king chooses by means of the Purohita’s *pravara*"—thus it is known. We shall first explain those belonging to the Bhṛgus, namely the Jamadagnya-Vatsas. Among them, there is a *pañcārṣeya*: Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya—that is, as for Jamadagni, as for Aurva, as for Āpnavāna, as for Cyavana, and as for Bhṛgu. Some, however, [perform] a *tryārṣeya*.

The lineage of Bhārgava-Urva-Jāmadagnya—namely, as Jāmadagnya, as Urva, and as Bhṛgu—is thus unmodified and common to all castes. For those of the Bālya, Śāyana, Vairohitya, Vaṭa, Maṇḍūṣa, Ācīnayogya, and Aṣṭrīṣeṇa families, there is a five-fold lineage: Bhārgava-Cyāvana-Āpnavāna-Ārṣīṣeṇa-Anūpa. [The term] Anūpa is like Ārṣīṣeṇa; Ārṣīṣeṇa is like Āpnavāna; Cyāvana is like Bhṛgu. Thus it is three-fold. However, some maintain a four-fold lineage: Bhārgava-Ārṣīṣeṇa-Anūpa, where Anūpa is like Ārṣīṣeṇa, and Ārṣīṣeṇa is like Bhṛgu.

Now, the Vaitahavyas, the Vaska-vadhūlas, and the Maunamaukas—of these, the *trārṣeya* (three-lineage) is: Bārgava, Vaitahavya, Sāvedasa; [the meaning being] "like Saveda, like Vitahavya, and like Bhṛgu. Now, the Gārtsnamadas and the Śunakas—of these, the *ekārṣeya* (single-lineage) is: Gārtsnamada; [the meaning being] "like Gṛtsamada," and thus the *adhvaryu*. Now, the Ādhyaras, the Adhrigavas, the Vainya-Pārthas—of these, the *tryārṣeya* is: Bārgava, Vainya, Pārtha; [the meaning being] "like Pṛthu, like Vena, and like Bhṛgu. These Bhṛgus have been explained. Now, therefore, [follow] the Aṅgirasas and the Āsyas.

O Gautamas, their triple *ṛṣi* lineage is Āṅgirasa, Ucathya, and Gautama—saying "Gautama" as one says "Gotama," saying "Ucathya" as one says "Aṅgiras. And those who are Gautamas, their triple *ṛṣi* lineage is Āṅgirasa, Ucathya, and Gautama—saying "Gautama" as one says "Gotama," saying "Ucathya" as one says "Aṅgiras," and saying "Aṅgiras" as one says "Aṅgiras. And those who are Gautamas... [the rest of the passage repeats the same formula].

The Śijas are Gautamas; their *trārṣeya* is: Āṅgirasa, Śijakākṣīvat—meaning "one who speaks like Kakṣīvat the Śija"—and Āṅgirasa, meaning "one who speaks like Aṅgiras. Now, the Vāmadevas are Gautamas; their *trārṣeya* is: Āṅgirasa, Vāmadeva, Bārhaduttha—meaning "one who speaks like Bṛhaduttha the Vāmadeva"—and Āṅgirasa, meaning "one who speaks like Aṅgiras. Now, for the Bharadvājas, the *trārṣeya* is: Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja—meaning "one who speaks like Bharadvāja," "one who speaks like Bṛhaspati," and "one who speaks like Aṅgiras. This [formula] remains unchanged.

Now, for the Vaiśyas of the Kuśva lineage, for all those whose names end in *stamba* or *stambha*, and for the families of the *dvaimuṣyāyaṇas*—such as the Śṛṅgas of the Śaiśiras, the Bharadvājas, and the Śṛṅgas who are Kātas of the Śaiśiras—their *pañcārṣeya* [pravara] is: Āṅgīrasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Kātya, and Ākṣīla. [The order is: like Akṣīla, like Kata, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, and like Aṅgiras. Or, there is one who has a *tryārṣeya* [pravara]: Āṅgīrasa, Kātya, and Ākṣīla. [The order is: like Akṣīla, like Kata, and like Aṅgiras.

For those of the Dartkṣa lineage, there is a five-ṛṣi [pravara]: Āṅgīrasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Vāndana, and Mātavacasa—namely, like Matavaca, like Vandana, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, and like Aṅgiras. Now, for the Gargas, there is a three-ṛṣi [pravara]: Āṅgīrasa, Gārgya, and Śainya—namely, like Śini, like Garga, and like Aṅgiras. Some, however, state the Bhāradvāja [lineage] in place of the Āṅgīrasa: Bhāradvāja, Gārgya, and Śainya—namely, like Śini, like Garga, and like Bharadvāja. Now, for the Kapilas, there is a three-ṛṣi [pravara]: Āṅgīrasa... [and so on].

The three *ṛṣis* of the *Sāma* lineage are *Ārṣeya*, *Tyārṣeya*, and *Tryārṣeya*; [the formula is] "O descendant of *Aṅgiras*, speak! O descendant of *Aṅgiras*, speak! Then, for those of the *Harita* lineage, there is a three-*ṛṣi* [formula]: *Āṅgirasa*, *Ambarīṣa*, and *Yauvanāśva*; [the formula is] "O descendant of *Yuvanāśva*, speak! O descendant of *Ambarīṣa*, speak! O descendant of *Aṅgiras*, speak! Some, however, say that for the *Mānthātṛ* lineage, in place of *Āṅgirasa*, [one says] *Mānthātṛ*, *Ambarīṣa*, and *Yauvanāśva*; [the formula is] "O descendant of *Yuvanāśva*, speak! O descendant of *Ambarīṣa*, speak! O descendant of *Manthātṛ*, speak!"

Now, for the Kutsas, there is a tri-ṛṣi lineage: Āṅgirasa, Manthātṛ, and Kautsa; that is, like Kutsa, like Manthātṛ, and like Aṅgiras. Then for the Virūpārathis, there is a tri-ṛṣi lineage: Āṅgirasa, Virūpa, and Pṛdāśva; that is, like Pṛdāśva, like Virūpa, and like Aṅgiras. For the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭras, there is one [lineage]: Āṅgirasa, Sthāna, and Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra; that is, like Pṛṣadaśva, like Virūpa, and like Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra. Now for the Mudgalas, there is a tri-ṛṣi lineage: Āṅgirasa, Bhaumya, and Aśva-maudgalya.

"Mudgala, Madhūbhūmyaśva, Vadaṅgiras"—thus [is the invocation] for Tryakṣu; "Tārkṣya, Bhūmyaśva, Maudgalya"—thus for the one in the place of Aṅgiras. "Mudgalavat, Bhūmyaśvavat, Tryakṣuvat"—thus for those whose lineage is Viṣṇuvṛddha; their triple *ṛṣi* lineage is: Āṅgirasa, Paurukutsya, Trasadasyava. "Trasadasyavat, Purukutsavat, Aṅgirasvat"—this very [formula] remains unchanged for Śaṭhamarṣaṇa, Bhadraṇa, Mandraṇa, Bādarāyaṇa, Aupamittha, Aupagavi, Sātviki, Sātvikāmi, Āruṇi, and Nitundina.

For the Ātris, there is a *tryārṣeya* [pravara]: Ātreya, Arcanānas, Śyāvāśva—namely, like Śyāvāśva, like Darbhavāvasa, like Atri. Now for the Dhanamjayas, there is a *tryārṣeya*: Ātreya, Arcanānas, Dhanamjaya—namely, like Dhanamjaya, like Arcanānas, like Atri. Now for the Ātithyas, there is a *tryārṣeya*: Ātreya, Arcanānas, Ātithya—namely, like Ātithi, like Arcanānas, like Atri. This same [pravara] is unmodified for the Vāmarathyas, Paumaṅgalas, and Bījavāpins.

Now, among the Viśvāmitras, there are the Devarātas: Cakita, Manuta, Taulaki, Bālaki, Yājñavalkya, Ulūka, Vṛbhraśīla, Śālāvata, Śālankāyana, Kālabava, and so forth. Their *trārṣeya* (three-lineage) formula is: Vaiśvāmitra, Daivarāta, Audala; [one says] "like Audala," "like Devarāta," and "like Viśvāmitra. Now, among the Śraumataka Māmakāyanas, their *tryārṣeya* is: Vaiśvāmitra, Daivaśravasa, Daivatarasa; [one says] "like Daivatarasa," "like Daivaśravas," and "like Viśvāmitra. Now, among the Yājñas, their *tryārṣeya* is: Vaiśvāmitra...

The Mādhucchandasas have Ājya as their *sūkta*; they are like Madhucchandas and Viśvāmitra. Now, the Dānastutis (Praises of Gifts) belong to the Mādhucchandasas; their *ṛṣi* lineage is threefold: Vaiśvāmitra, Mādhucchandasa, and Dhānañjaya. They are like Dhanañjaya, Madhucchandas, and Viśvāmitra. Now, the Aṣṭakas are Lohitas; their *ṛṣi* lineage is twofold: Vaiśvāmitra and Aṣṭaka. They are like Aṣṭaka and Viśvāmitra. Now, the Pūraṇas cause [the hymns] to be recited; their *ṛṣi* lineage is twofold: Vaiśvāmitra...

The Kātyākṣīlas have three *ṛṣis*: Vaiśvāmitra, Aghamarṣaṇa, and Kauśīke; they are like Kuśika, like Aghamarṣaṇa, and like Viśvāmitra. Next, the Kaśyapas have three *ṛṣis*: Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, and Naidhruva; they are like Nidhruva, like Avatsāra, and like Kaśyapa. Then, the Rephas have three *ṛṣis*: Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, and Raipha; they are like Raipha, like Avatsāra, and like Kaśyapa.

Now, for the Śāṇḍilas, there is a two-ṛṣi lineage: "daivalāsite" (O descendant of Devala and Asita), [the Hotṛ] says "asita vat devala vat"; for a three-ṛṣi lineage, some say: "kāśyapadaivalāsite" (O descendant of Kaśyapa, Devala, and Asita), [the Hotṛ] says "asita vat devala vat kaśyapa vat. However, according to this rule, they are indeed two-ṛṣi lineages; the Vāsiṣṭhas are not one-ṛṣi lineages, except for the Parāśaras. For the Vāsiṣṭhas, the Hotṛ says "vāsiṣṭha" and the Adhvaryu says "vasiṣṭha vat. Some, however, prescribe a three-ṛṣi lineage for the Vāsiṣṭhas: "aindrapramathabhāradvāsū" (O descendant of Bharadvāja, Indrapramada, and Vasiṣṭha), [the Hotṛ] says "bharadvāja vat indrapramada vat vasiṣṭha vat. Now, [regarding the next]:

For the Parāśaras, there is a tri-ārṣeya lineage: Vāsiṣṭha, Śāktya, and Pārāśarya—namely, as for Parāśara, Śakti, and Vasiṣṭha. Now, for the Kuṇḍikas, there is a tri-ārṣeya lineage: Vāsiṣṭha, Maitrāvaruṇa, and Kauṇḍinya.

[The lineage] of the Kuṇḍinas is like that of Mitrāvaruṇa and Vasiṣṭha: *siṃkṛti*, *pūti*, *māṣāṇām*—this is the three-fold lineage (*trārṣeya*): Śāktya, Sāṃkṛtya, Gaurivīta; [the invocation is] "Gaurivīta, Vatsaṃkṛti, Vatsaṃkṛti, Śāktya. Now, for the Agastyas: the Hotṛ priest invokes *ekārṣeya* as "Agastya," and the Adhvaryu as "Agastya. Their three-fold lineage (*tryārṣeya*) is: Muhekarḍhya, Āgastya, Dārḍhyacyuta; [the invocation is] "Idhmavāha"—[the priests] should choose "Idhmavāha" as their name. For these, there is only one single *pravara*: "Mānava, Aiḍa, Paurūravasa"; [the invocation is] "Purūravas, Aiḍa, Mānava."

Regarding those whose ancestral lineage (*pravara*) consists of the Vṛtra-slayers, they should choose the Purohita as their *pravara*. Now, for those whose ancestral lineage has the Sun-god as their Purohita, they should choose that Purohita as their *pravara*; thus, by this rule, the commoners (*viś*) have a single ancestral lineage (*ekārṣeya*). The Pratiprasthātṛ says, "Vat," and the Adhvaryu says, "Vatphavat. Then, one who is of known kinship should recite the ancestral lineage of his teacher; if he is the son of such-and-such (an *amupyāyaṇa*), he should recite the ancestral lineage of his teacher. Furthermore, the Tāṇḍins prescribe a single ancestral lineage applicable to all classes (*sārvavarṇika*): "Mānava" (the descendant of Manu).
The Adhvaryu follows the Hotṛ, saying, "O Mānava, come; O Prajā, come; O Brāhmaṇa, come; O Brāhmaṇa, come. Om, Tat Sat.
Salutations to the lotus-feet of the venerable sage Āpastamba.
Thus concludes the investigation into the *Gotra* and *Pravara* sections.
Salutations to the venerable gurus.
The procedure for the application of mantras beginning with the Rudrādhyāya;
the sequence for the recitation (japa), fire-oblation (homa), and other rites to be performed during the Rudrādhyāya.
One should meditate upon Śiva, the Lord of Gods, who is mounted upon his bull, the sole cause of all the worlds,
praised by Brahmā and the other gods, and accompanied by Pārvatī.
By the mere recitation of this *Rudra-samudaya*, all perfections (*siddhi*) are attained.
By bathing at the three periods of the day and performing the recitation, one becomes purified from the five great sins (*pañca-mahāpātaka*).
Now follows the ritual application (*prayoga*) for the fulfillment of all desires, as taught by Śaunaka.

Then, having performed the subsequent rites such as the placement of mantras (*nyāsa*) according to the previously mentioned procedure, one should prepare water-pots (*kalaśas*) measuring one *prastha* each, or as many as the number of constellations (*nakṣatras*), filled with water along with fragrances and flowers. Having worshipped the Deity according to the aforementioned rite, one should offer oblations of clarified butter (*ājya-huti*) into the fire beside the Deity while reciting the mantras of the first section of the *Rudra-praśna*, and then mutter the *Rudra-ekādaśinī*. At the conclusion of that recitation, one should mutter each of the eleven sections beginning with "O Agni and Viṣṇu" (*agnāviṣṇū*).

Then one should bathe [the deity] with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*). Then with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Then follows the preliminary service (*upacāra*) with the mantra "A namaste. Then, according to one's capacity, one should feed Brahmins who are knowers of the Rudra-veda; all desires will be fulfilled. Alternatively, one should offer milk-rice (*pāyasa*) into the fire according to the number prescribed for the Rudra-mahārudra or any other Rudra rite; one attains all desires. Or else, in this very manner, according to one's ability, one should offer oblations of milk, ghee, and milk-rice together.

Now, this same procedure applies to the rites of expulsion (*uccāṭana*) performed in a location involving the use of a concealing cloth, planetary influences, and so forth. One should commence all undertakings with the utterance of *phaṭ*. Furthermore, for one desiring a kingdom, one should offer one hundred thousand lotuses, fragrant flowers, and *kotsalas*—anointed with both types of sandalwood paste—to the head of the Lord Maheśvara, using the mantra "O Discharger of the Bow. Thus, the king attains royal fortune.

With the mantra "namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ," one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of sesame and rice grains smeared with clarified butter; one attains sovereignty. Now, another method is stated by Bodhāyana: desiring a kingdom, one should offer ten thousand oblations of barley grains smeared with clarified butter while reciting any one of the Rudra, Mahārudra, or Atirudra mantras according to the number prescribed for their recitation (japya). Now, for one desiring prosperity (śrī): having recited any one of the Rudra, Mahārudra, or Atirudra mantras, one should offer ten thousand oblations of milk-rice (pāyasa); one obtains prosperity.

For one desiring wealth: with the mantra "imā rudrāya," one should offer a hundred thousand oblations of sesame seeds. Then, in the *Kālikā Purāṇa*, Sanatkumāra says: "First, O twice-born one, having performed the preliminary rites (*aṅgas*) and bathed in his own body, the devotee should thereafter worship Mahādeva according to the prescribed rules. Having bathed one Linga on a riverbank and another with water, and again having bathed Śambhu with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and a hundred fruits, he should then meditate upon that Lord of the Universe. For the sake of obtaining Gorocanā, he should smear the heart of the Lord with devotion."

Then, one should worship the Lord with unblemished bilva leaves produced from the *śrīvṛkṣa* tree, which are fresh, not stale, glossy, and sprinkled with water. One should worship that Great Lord for eleven days according to this procedure; O Lord of Gods, listen further to the ritual involving the *stava*. For the first eleven days, at the conclusion of the worship, one should perform a fire-oblation (*homa*) using bilva leaves mixed with clarified butter, standing facing the southern direction. Likewise, one should worship with blue lotuses and again with fragrant *padma* flowers.

One should perform a *homamarcā* for eleven days, burning *guggulu* resin mixed with clarified butter daily, which is dear to Hara; at the conclusion of the worship, through supreme devotion, there shall be an accumulation of wealth for him. When he desires wealth, he should then recite the *vanaspati* mantras over the linga; by meditating on Śiva, they certainly attain the state of being offered as oblations (*homatā*). One should recite [the mantra] over a tree that has flowers, or over a *bilva* tree outside the linga; by revolving it many times, that tree attains the state of gold (*hematā*).

Having gone to the Tīrthaka-sakhala and having recited the Rudra-mantras many times, one should recite them again at the middle-japa; O Kṛṣṇa, the stones shall turn into gold. Taking refuge in Mahārva and supporting oneself there day by day, one should recite for eleven days; thus one will obtain abundant treasure. He who offers oblations of Vetasī wood soaked in the three sweets (trimadhu) at the end of that [period], for him there shall arise at its conclusion abundant and great wealth.

Trees such as the *madhūka* and others grow when embraced on the eleventh day [of the lunar fortnight] and attain a golden state; this is the truth, there is no doubt in this matter. Alternatively, having resorted to a self-manifested (*svayambhu*) linga facing the western direction, one should recite [mantras] for eleven days while covering it with lotuses. One should not look upon or touch animals, nor those who are censurable. Whomever one sees, that person shall depart; on the twelfth day, there will be gold. Now, another method: beginning from the eighth day of the dark fortnight until the fourth day of the dark fortnight...

Having spread out a sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) or a seat of *arka* grass, the wise man should perform recitation (*japa*). With the mantra "Salutation to the Blue-necked One" (*namo astu nīlagrīvāya*), he should offer a crow fed with ghee to the Lord (*Īśvara*) after it has been consecrated one thousand times. A thousand *kārṣāpaṇa* coins will then be produced. Now another [method]: With the mantra "Loosen the bow" (*pramuñca dhanvana*), he should offer eight thousand oblations of prepared food into the fire along with *sahānasa*. His wealth will become uninterrupted and inexhaustible. Now another [method]:

"One should offer ten thousand oblations of sesame seeds with the mantra 'namevaḥ kirikebhyaḥ'; a thousand *kārṣāpaṇa* coins will be produced," so it is stated in the *Kālikā-purāṇa*. Now, regarding one who desires food, Śaunaka says: "With both [mantras] beginning with 'asau yaḥ tāmra,' one should worship the Sun at sunrise and sunset every day; inexhaustible food attends him. Now, Bodhāyana says:

Having recited either the *Rudra*, the *Mahārudra*, or any one of the Rudra-hymns over *utumbara* fuel-sticks, clarified butter, or parched grains (*akṣata*) the prescribed number of times, one should offer oblations; then food will be produced. Now, Śaunaka [speaks] regarding the ritual for rain: "With the hymn beginning 'Asau yaḥ tāmraḥ,' one should offer ten thousand oblations of water-plants, *śākya*, or *vaitasa* fuel-sticks. Or, one should offer ten thousand oblations of these [fuel-sticks] smeared with molasses and milk. The Lord Āditya releases the rain. Having propitiated the Deity according to the previously mentioned procedure, having offered red, yellow, and black oblations (*bali*) in all directions, and having recited the *Pudraikādaśinī* eleven times, one should perform the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) with the mantra beginning "Ārāt te goghna," and then recite that same mantra a thousand times. If one is afflicted by disease, one should give a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) to a Brāhmaṇa on a Sunday and have him cause the mantra to be recited a thousand times; thus one is liberated from diseases and becomes a hundred-year-old. Now, regarding one desiring a son, Śaunaka says:

One should offer ten thousand oblations of *vaṭa* wood with the mantra "pariṇo rudrasya. A long-lived son is born. Now, for one desiring cattle, it is the same [procedure]. One should offer ten thousand oblations of fuel-sticks (*samidh*) made of *vikaṅkata* and *udumbara* wood, smeared with curd, with the mantra "namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ. He becomes the owner of infinite cattle, and his cows do not diminish. Alternatively, with this very same mantra, one should offer eleven oblations of hundred *arka* leaves with cow's milk; eleven cows are produced.

Alternatively, he himself has stated this: having installed a clay liṅga at Mahācatuṣpada, one should bathe it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Having consecrated it with the mantra "samovaḥ kirikebhyaḥ," one should offer bilva fruits for two days with the mantra "mānastoke. At Dakṣiṇāmūrti, one should take vacā and *samartha* fruit, grind them into a very fine powder, and place it in a copper vessel.

Having mixed [the substance] with monkey-ghee and empowered it with the *pradeśinī* finger, one should drink it; thus one's speech becomes unassailable. Furthermore, with the mantra beginning "punastvādityā rudrā vasavaḥ," one should offer oblations (*juhuyāt*) a hundred thousand times; garments will flow forth [as a result]. Now, for one desiring subjugation (*vaśya*), Bodhāyana says: having recited the *rudraikādaśinī*, the *rudra*, the *mahārudra*, and the *atirudra*, one should offer white flowers; this brings everything under one's control.

Now, suppose someone who has mastered his senses desires to bring the entire world under his control. Standing in water reaching up to his navel, he should mutter many Rudras while performing the worship of Śambhu and undertaking the *rādhāya* vow. Facing the sun, he should constantly recite the Rudras. As that wise man of conquered senses recites the Rudras, the bull-bannered Lord, the giver of boons who is affectionate toward his devotees, appears before him. [Thus spoke] Śaunaka regarding one who desires freedom from disease.

One should offer ten thousand oblations of sesame seeds with the mantra "mano mahantam. This brings about health for children and the warding off of calamities. Furthermore, when every kind of fear has arisen, one should present the sacrificial offerings (bali), perform the sixteen-fold service again with the mantra "mīḍhuṣṭama," and recite or cause a knower of the Rudra-mantras to recite the Rudraikādaśinī eleven times; thus one is liberated from all fears—of this there is no doubt.

One should offer ten thousand oblations each of curd, honey, and milk-rice with the mantra "imāg rudrā. All fears are thereby pacified. Now, one desiring peace, having performed the placement of mantras (*nyāsa*) upon the deity and so forth according to the previously stated procedure, and having worshipped the God, should appoint a Brahmin learned in the *Rudra* as the preceptor (*ācārya*). Having approached a self-manifested (*svayambhū*) linga and performed worship there according to this very same procedure, he should bathe it with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*), perform an oblation of clarified butter (*ājyahoma*) with the first section (*anuvāka*), and fully honor the God.

One should perform the recitation (*japa*) of the eleven sections (*anuvākas*) beginning with "Obeisance to you, O Rudra, to your wrath" (*namaste rudra manyave*). At the end of the recitation, while pouring the continuous stream of ghee (*dhārānūsrāva*), one should recite each of the eleven sections beginning with "O Agni and Viṣṇu, being of one mind" (*agnāviṣṇo sajoṣasā*) one by one.

Again, having bathed [the deity] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and worshipped the God, and having offered an oblation (naivedya) consisting of various kinds of food, one should worship four full jars containing the five earths, the five herbs, and the five gems, adorned with unbroken rice, scents, incense, and so forth. Having wrapped them in white cloth and meditated upon the peace-mantra "May the wind blow auspiciously for us," and having recited it, one should cause the consecration (abhiṣeka) to be performed. Thus peace is attained; thereafter, one's own self becomes peaceful.

One should give the preceptor a pair of white garments, a cow, and gold; one should also feed Brāhmaṇas, and thus peace is attained—so says Śaunaka again. With the mantra "mā no mahāntam," one should offer ten thousand oblations of clarified butter. Every year, during the festival procession, one should offer ten thousand oblations. When this is done, there is peace for one's own children, whether they be young or old.

With these two [mantras], "namo bhavāya" and "namo jyeṣṭhāya," one should empower ashes with the mantra and provide protection for those seized by Kumāra-graha and other such spirits. At night, one should tie a lock of hair; thus, there will be no fear of Kumāra-graha and other spirits. With the mantra "mīḍhuṣṭama śivatama," one should mentally recite [it] during great danger, danger from thieves, danger from fire, or when life is at stake; one returns in safety. With the mantra "imāṃ rudrāya," one should offer oblations a hundred thousand times with gold and dūrvā sprouts.

Even one whose life has reached its end becomes long-lived upon the destruction of a great fever. With the four verses beginning with *namaste rudra manyave*, one should offer ten thousand oblations of barley, wheat, *gavīdhuka* grain, and wild sesame seeds, mixed with curds, honey, and clarified butter, verse by verse. Within eleven or twelve nights, one pacifies the wind. The protection against all [diseases] should be performed with the verse *adyavoca dadhivaktā*.

Having consecrated mustard seeds with the mantra seven times, one should scatter them in the four cardinal directions and the ten directions; thus protection is established. For one who is traveling, well-being is attained. With mustard seeds, one may liberate [a person] from the Brahma-rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, and other such beings. Having consecrated a protective amulet (*pratisara*) a thousand times with the verse "yatā rudra śivā tanūḥ," and having tied eleven knots, one should bind it on the hands of children and pregnant women.

And pregnant women shall thrive in comfort. There is also the destruction of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas. With [the mantra] "He who is with thousands," one should worship the God with red garments, a red turban, red garlands, and red unguents.

In a cremation ground, at a solitary tree, on a riverbank, or in a forest at a crossroads, one should grind cotton and rice together with a large amount of [oil] and smear it. Having prepared an image of an enemy—even of a Yakṣa, a Rākṣasa, or any other foe—using barley flour mixed with bitter oil, and having consecrated it eleven times with the *tri-mantra* over the blazing fire of the cremation ground, one should place the image in the southern part of the site and pierce its vital points with each individual arrow. This instantly destroys an enemy, whether he has arrived suddenly or is already present throughout the world.
